s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest and back pain with progressive dyspnea and electrocardiogram changes
salient_findings: Persistent chest and back pain
Dyspnea on exertion
Diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR
Elevated cardiac troponin I level
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle
Cystic mass above the left atrium
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
History of hypertension
Chest discomfort started two months prior
Dyspnea on exertion gradually worsened
Electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm
Occasional premature ventricular complexes
Cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle
Contrast-enhanced CT scan showed a cystic mass above the left atrium
Mass had heterogeneous attenuation on noncontrast images
Mass exhibited slight contrast enhancement
Patient developed transient cardiogenic shock after CT
Cardiogenic shock responded to noradrenaline support

shortlist.label: Cardiac Tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium and transient cardiogenic shock

shortlist.label: Left Atrial Myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and electrocardiogram changes

shortlist.label: Myocardial Infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Electrocardiogram changes and diffuse ST-segment depression

raw.rationale: The presence of a cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and slight contrast enhancement on CT scan, along with the patient's symptoms of chest discomfort, dyspnea on exertion, and cardiac troponin elevation, is most consistent with a left atrial myxoma causing obstructive symptoms and potentially embolic events.

rejected.label: Cardiac Tamponade
rejected.why: There is no mention of a significant pericardial effusion or equalization of diastolic pressures across all cardiac chambers.

rejected.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated troponin and ECG changes, the primary issue appears to be related to the mass effect from the cystic mass rather than coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction
rejected.why: The diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle and elevated troponin could suggest myocardial infarction, but the presence of a cystic mass above the left atrium points towards a different primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: There is no mention of pericardial inflammation or characteristic ECG changes of pericarditis, such as widespread ST elevation without reciprocal changes.
